params.desc_en: Determines which of the accuracy measures Horizontal position, Vertical Position and Speed are used to calculate the weighting on each GPS receiver when soft switching has been selected by setting GPS_AUTO_SWITCH to 2(Blend)

params.name: GPS_CAN_NODEID1
params.desc_en: GPS Node id for first-discovered GPS.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS1_CAN_NODEID.

params.name: GPS_CAN_NODEID2
params.desc_en: GPS Node id for second-discovered GPS.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS2_CAN_NODEID.

params.name: GPS_COM_PORT
params.desc_en: The physical COM port on the connected device, currently only applies to SBF and GSOF GPS,Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS1_COM_PORT.

params.name: GPS_COM_PORT2
params.desc_en: The physical COM port on the connected device, currently only applies to SBF and GSOF GPS.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS1_COM_PORT.

params.name: GPS_DELAY_MS
params.desc_en: Controls the amount of GPS measurement delay that the autopilot compensates for. Set to zero to use the default delay for the detected GPS type.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS1_DELAY_MS.

params.name: GPS_DELAY_MS2
params.desc_en: Controls the amount of GPS measurement delay that the autopilot compensates for. Set to zero to use the default delay for the detected GPS type.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS2_DELAY_MS.

params.name: GPS_DRV_OPTIONS
params.desc_en: Additional backend specific options

bitmask.en: Use UART2 for moving baseline on ublox
Use base station for GPS yaw on SBF
Use dedicated CAN port b/w GPSes for moving baseline
Use ellipsoid height instead of AMSL
Override GPS satellite health of L5 band from L1 health
Enable RTCM full parse even for a single channel
Disable automatic full RTCM parsing when RTCM seen on more than one channel
Force UBlox Config Get/Set for configuration then automatic configuration for Serial GPSes only

params.name: GPS_GNSS_MODE
params.desc_en: Bitmask for what GNSS system to use on the first GPS (all unchecked or zero to leave GPS as configured).Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS1_GNSS_MODE.

params.name: GPS_GNSS_MODE2
params.desc_en: Bitmask for what GNSS system to use on the second GPS (all unchecked or zero to leave GPS as configured). Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS2_GNSS_MODE

params.name: GPS_HDOP_GOOD
params.desc_en: GPS Hdop value at or below this value represent a good position. Used for pre-arm checks

params.name: GPS_INJECT_TO
params.desc_en: The GGS can send raw serial packets to inject data to multiple GPSes.

params.name: GPS_MB1_OFS_X
params.desc_en: X position of the base (primary) GPS antenna in body frame from the position of the 2nd antenna. Positive X is forward of the 2nd antenna. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.This is renamed in 4.6 and later to GPSx_MB_OFS_X.

params.name: GPS_MB1_OFS_Y
params.desc_en: Y position of the base (primary) GPS antenna in body frame from the position of the 2nd antenna. Positive Y is to the right of the 2nd antenna. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.This is renamed in 4.6 and later to GPSx_MB_OFS_Y.

params.name: GPS_MB1_OFS_Z
params.desc_en: Z position of the base (primary) GPS antenna in body frame from the position of the 2nd antenna. Positive Z is down from the 2nd antenna. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.This is renamed in 4.6 and later to GPSx_MB_OFS_Z.

params.name: GPS_MB1_TYPE
params.desc_en: Controls the type of moving base used if using moving base.This is renamed in 4.6 and later to GPSx_MB_TYPE.

params.name: GPS_MB2_OFS_X
params.desc_en: X position of the base (primary) GPS antenna in body frame from the position of the 2nd antenna. Positive X is forward of the 2nd antenna. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.This is renamed in 4.6 and later to GPSx_MB_OFS_X.

params.name: GPS_MB2_OFS_Y
params.desc_en: Y position of the base (primary) GPS antenna in body frame from the position of the 2nd antenna. Positive Y is to the right of the 2nd antenna. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.This is renamed in 4.6 and later to GPSx_MB_OFS_Y.

params.name: GPS_MB2_OFS_Z
params.desc_en: Z position of the base (primary) GPS antenna in body frame from the position of the 2nd antenna. Positive Z is down from the 2nd antenna. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.This is renamed in 4.6 and later to GPSx_MB_OFS_Z.

params.name: GPS_MB2_TYPE
params.desc_en: Controls the type of moving base used if using moving base.This is renamed in 4.6 and later to GPSx_MB_TYPE.

params.name: GPS_MIN_ELEV
params.desc_en: This sets the minimum elevation of satellites above the horizon for them to be used for navigation. Setting this to -100 leaves the minimum elevation set to the GPS modules default.

params.name: GPS_NAVFILTER
params.desc_en: Navigation filter engine setting

params.name: GPS_POS1_X
params.desc_en: X position of the first GPS antenna in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS1_POS_X.

params.name: GPS_POS1_Y
params.desc_en: Y position of the first GPS antenna in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS1_POS_Y.

params.name: GPS_POS1_Z
params.desc_en: Z position of the first GPS antenna in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS1_POS_Z.

params.name: GPS_POS2_X
params.desc_en: X position of the second GPS antenna in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS2_POS_X.

params.name: GPS_POS2_Y
params.desc_en: Y position of the second GPS antenna in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS2_POS_Y.

params.name: GPS_POS2_Z
params.desc_en: Z position of the second GPS antenna in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin. Use antenna phase centroid location if provided by the manufacturer.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS2_POS_Z.

params.name: GPS_PRIMARY
params.desc_en: This GPS will be used when GPS_AUTO_SWITCH is 0 and used preferentially with GPS_AUTO_SWITCH = 4.

params.name: GPS_RATE_MS
params.desc_en: Controls how often the GPS should provide a position update. Lowering below 5Hz(default) is not allowed. Raising the rate above 5Hz usually provides little benefit and for some GPS (eg Ublox M9N) can severely impact performance.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS1_RATE_MS

params.name: GPS_RATE_MS2
params.desc_en: Controls how often the GPS should provide a position update. Lowering below 5Hz(default) is not allowed. Raising the rate above 5Hz usually provides little benefit and for some GPS (eg Ublox M9N) can severely impact performance.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS2_RATE_MS

params.name: GPS_RAW_DATA
params.desc_en: Handles logging raw data; on uBlox chips that support raw data this will log RXM messages into logger; on Septentrio this will log on the equipment's SD card and when set to 2, the autopilot will try to stop logging after disarming and restart after arming

values.en: Only log every five samples (uBlox only)

params.name: GPS_SAVE_CFG
params.desc_en: Determines whether the configuration for this GPS should be written to non-volatile memory on the GPS. Currently working for UBlox 6 series and above.

params.name: GPS_SBAS_MODE
params.desc_en: This sets the SBAS (satellite based augmentation system) mode if available on this GPS. If set to 2 then the SBAS mode is not changed in the GPS. Otherwise the GPS will be reconfigured to enable/disable SBAS. Disabling SBAS may be worthwhile in some parts of the world where an SBAS signal is available but the baseline is too long to be useful.

params.name: GPS_SBP_LOGMASK
params.desc_en: Masked with the SBP msg_type field to determine whether SBR1/SBR2 data is logged

params.name: GPS_TYPE
params.desc_en: GPS type of 1st GPS.Renamed in 4.6 and later to GPS1_TYPE

params.name: GPS_TYPE2
params.desc_en: GPS type of 2nd GPS

params.name: GRIP_AUTOCLOSE
params.desc_en: Time in seconds that gripper close the gripper after opening; 0 to disable

params.name: GRIP_CAN_ID
params.desc_en: Refer to https://docs.zubax.com/opengrab_epm_v3#UAVCAN_interface

params.name: GRIP_ENABLE
params.desc_en: Gripper enable/disable

params.name: GRIP_GRAB
params.desc_en: PWM value in microseconds sent to Gripper to initiate grabbing the cargo

params.name: GRIP_NEUTRAL
params.desc_en: PWM value in microseconds sent to grabber when not grabbing or releasing

params.name: GRIP_REGRAB
params.desc_en: Time in seconds that EPM gripper will regrab the cargo to ensure grip has not weakened; 0 to disable

params.name: GRIP_RELEASE
params.desc_en: PWM value in microseconds sent to Gripper to release the cargo

params.name: GRIP_TYPE
params.desc_en: Gripper enable/disable

params.name: GUID_OPTIONS
params.desc_en: Options that can be applied to change guided mode behaviour

bitmask.en: Waypoint navigation used for position targets

params.name: GUID_TIMEOUT
params.desc_en: Guided mode timeout after which vehicle will stop or return to level if no updates are received from caller. Only applicable during any combination of velocity, acceleration, angle control, and/or angular rate control

params.name: H_COL2YAW
params.desc_en: Feed-forward compensation to automatically add rudder input when collective pitch is increased. Can be positive or negative depending on mechanics.

params.name: H_COL2_MAX
params.desc_en: Highest possible servo position in PWM microseconds for swashplate 2

params.name: H_COL2_MIN
params.desc_en: Lowest possible servo position in PWM microseconds for swashplate 2

params.name: H_COL_ANG_MAX
params.desc_en: Maximum collective blade pitch angle in deg that corresponds to the PWM set for maximum collective pitch (H_COL_MAX).

params.name: H_COL_ANG_MIN
params.desc_en: Minimum collective blade pitch angle in deg that corresponds to the PWM set for minimum collective pitch (H_COL_MIN).

params.name: H_COL_HOVER
params.desc_en: Collective needed to hover expressed as a number from 0 to 1 where 0 is H_COL_MIN and 1 is H_COL_MAX

params.name: H_COL_LAND_MIN
params.display: Collective Blade Pitch Minimum when Landed
params.desc_en: Minimum collective blade pitch angle when landed in degrees for non-manual collective modes (i.e. modes that use altitude hold).

params.name: H_COL_MAX
params.desc_en: Highest possible servo position in PWM microseconds for the swashplate

params.name: H_COL_MIN
params.desc_en: Lowest possible servo position in PWM microseconds for the swashplate

params.name: H_COL_ZERO_THRST
params.display: Collective Blade Pitch at Zero Thrust
params.desc_en: Collective blade pitch angle at zero thrust in degrees. For symetric airfoil blades this value is zero deg. For chambered airfoil blades this value is typically negative.

params.name: H_CYC_MAX
params.desc_en: Maximum cyclic pitch angle of the swash plate. There are no units to this parameter. This should be adjusted to get the desired cyclic blade pitch for the pitch and roll axes. Typically this should be 6-7 deg (measured blade pitch angle difference between stick centered and stick max deflection.

params.name: H_DCP_SCALER
params.desc_en: Scaling factor applied to the differential-collective-pitch

params.name: H_DCP_TRIM
params.desc_en: Removes I term bias due to center of gravity offsets or discrepancies between rotors in swashplate setup. If DCP axis has I term bias while hovering in calm winds, use value of bias in DCP_TRIM to re-center I term.

params.name: H_DCP_YAW
params.desc_en: Feed-forward compensation to automatically add yaw input when differential collective pitch is applied. Disabled for intermeshing mode.

params.name: H_DDFP_BAT_IDX
params.display: DDFP Tail Rotor Battery compensation index
params.desc_en: Which battery monitor should be used for doing compensation

params.name: H_DDFP_BAT_V_MAX
params.desc_en: Battery voltage compensation maximum voltage (voltage above this will have no additional scaling effect on thrust). Recommend 4.2 * cell count, 0 = Disabled

params.name: H_DDFP_BAT_V_MIN
params.desc_en: Battery voltage compensation minimum voltage (voltage below this will have no additional scaling effect on thrust). Recommend 3.3 * cell count, 0 = Disabled

params.name: H_DDFP_SPIN_MAX
params.display: DDFP Tail Rotor Motor Spin maximum
params.desc_en: Point at which the thrust saturates expressed as a number from 0 to 1 in the entire output range

params.name: H_DDFP_SPIN_MIN
params.display: DDFP Tail Rotor Motor Spin minimum
params.desc_en: Point at which the thrust starts expressed as a number from 0 to 1 in the entire output range.

params.name: H_DDFP_THST_EXPO
params.display: DDFP Tail Rotor Thrust Curve Expo
params.desc_en: Tail rotor DDFP motor thrust curve exponent (0.0 for linear to 1.0 for second order curve)

params.name: H_DUAL_MODE
params.desc_en: Sets the dual mode of the heli, either as tandem, transverse, or intermeshing/coaxial.

params.name: H_FLYBAR_MODE
params.desc_en: Flybar present or not. Affects attitude controller used during ACRO flight mode

params.name: H_GYR_GAIN
params.desc_en: PWM in microseconds sent to external gyro on an servo/output whose function is Motor7 when tail type is Servo w/ ExtGyro

params.name: H_GYR_GAIN_ACRO
params.desc_en: PWM in microseconds sent to external gyro on an servo/output whose function is Motor7 when tail type is Servo w/ ExtGyro in mode ACRO instead of H_GYR_GAIN. A value of zero means to use H_GYR_GAIN

params.name: H_HOVER_LEARN
params.desc_en: Enable/Disable automatic learning of hover collective

params.name: H_OPTIONS
params.desc_en: Bitmask of heli options. Bit 0 changes how the pitch, roll, and yaw axis integrator term is managed for low speed and takeoff/landing. In AC 4.0 and earlier, scheme uses a leaky integrator for ground speeds less than 5 m/s and won't let the steady state integrator build above ILMI. The integrator is allowed to build to the ILMI value when it is landed. The other integrator management scheme bases integrator limiting on takeoff and landing. Whenever the aircraft is landed the integrator is set to zero. When the aicraft is airborne, the integrator is only limited by IMAX.

params.name: H_RSC_AROT_ENBL
params.desc_en: Allows you to enable (1) or disable (0) the autorotation functionality within the Rotor Speed Controller.

params.name: H_RSC_AROT_IDLE
params.desc_en: Idle throttle used for during autotoration. For external governors, this would be set to a value that is within the autorotation window of the governer/ESC to enable fast spool-up, when bailing out of an autorotation. Set 0 to disable.

params.name: H_RSC_AROT_RAMP
params.display: Time for in-flight power re-engagement when exiting autorotations
params.desc_en: When exiting an autorotation in a bailout manoeuvre, this is the time in seconds for the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) to ramp from idle (H_RSC_AROT_IDLE) to flight throttle setting when motor interlock is re-enabled. When using an ESC with an autorotation bailout function, this parameter should be set to 0.1 (minimum value).

params.name: H_RSC_AROT_RUNUP
params.display: Time allowed for in-flight power re-engagement
params.desc_en: When exiting an autorotation in a bailout manoeuvre, this is the expected time in seconds for the main rotor to reach full speed after motor interlock is enabled. Must be at least one second longer than the H_RSC_AROT_RAMP time that is set. This timer should be set for at least the amount of time it takes to get your helicopter to full flight power. Failure to heed this warning could result in early entry into autonomously controlled collective modes (e.g. alt hold, loiter, etc), whereby the collective could be raised before the engine has reached full power, with a subsequently dangerous slowing of head speed.

params.name: H_RSC_CLDWN_TIME
params.desc_en: Will provide a fast idle for engine cooldown by raising the Ground Idle speed setting by 50% for the number of seconds the timer is set for. A setting of zero disables the fast idle. This feature will only apply after the runup complete has been declared. This will not extend the time before ground idle is declared, which triggers engine shutdown for autonomous landings.

params.name: H_RSC_CRITICAL
params.desc_en: Percentage of normal rotor speed where flight is no longer possible. However currently the rotor runup/rundown is estimated using the RSC_RUNUP_TIME parameter. Estimated rotor speed increases/decreases between 0 (rotor stopped) to 1 (rotor at normal speed) in the RSC_RUNUP_TIME in seconds. This parameter should be set so that the estimated rotor speed goes below critical in approximately 3 seconds. So if you had a 10 second runup time then set RSC_CRITICAL to 70%.

params.name: H_RSC_GOV_COMP
params.desc_en: Adjusts the autothrottle governor torque compensator that determines how fast the governor will adjust the base torque reference to compensate for changes in density altitude. If RPM is low or high by more than 2-5 RPM, increase this setting by 1% at a time until the governor speed matches your RPM setting. Setting the compensator too high can result in surging and throttle "hunting". Do not make large adjustments at one time

params.name: H_RSC_GOV_DROOP
params.desc_en: AutoThrottle governor droop response under load, normal settings of 0-50%. Higher value is quicker response to large speed changes due to load but may cause surging. Adjust this to be as aggressive as possible without getting surging or RPM over-run when the governor responds to large load changes on the rotor system

params.name: H_RSC_GOV_FF
params.desc_en: Feedforward governor gain to throttle response during sudden loading/unloading of the rotor system. If RPM drops excessively during full collective climb with the droop response set correctly, increase the governor feedforward.

params.name: H_RSC_GOV_RANGE
params.desc_en: RPM range +/- governor rpm reference setting where governor is operational. If speed sensor fails or rpm falls outside of this range, the governor will disengage and return to throttle curve. Recommended range is 100

params.name: H_RSC_GOV_RPM
params.desc_en: Main rotor RPM that governor maintains when engaged

params.name: H_RSC_GOV_TORQUE
params.desc_en: Adjusts the engine's percentage of torque rise on autothrottle during ramp-up to governor speed. The torque rise will determine how fast the rotor speed will ramp up when rotor speed reaches 50% of the rotor RPM setting. The sequence of events engaging the governor is as follows: Throttle ramp time will engage the clutch and start the main rotor turning. The collective should be at flat pitch and the throttle curve set to provide at least 50% of normal RPM at flat pitch. The autothrottle torque limiter will automatically activate and start accelerating the main rotor. If the autothrottle consistently fails to accelerate the main rotor during ramp-in due to engine tune or other factors, then increase the torque limiter setting. NOTE: throttle ramp time and throttle curve should be tuned using RSC_MODE Throttle Curve before using RSC_MODE AutoThrottle

params.name: H_RSC_IDLE
params.desc_en: Throttle output (HeliRSC Servo) in percent while armed but motor interlock is disabled (throttle hold on). FOR COMBUSTION ENGINES. Sets the engine ground idle throttle percentage with clutch disengaged. This must be set to zero for electric helicopters under most situations. If the ESC has an autorotation window this can be set to keep the autorotation window open in the ESC. Consult the operating manual for your ESC to set it properly for this purpose

params.name: H_RSC_MODE
params.desc_en: Selects the type of rotor speed control used to determine throttle output to the HeliRSC servo channel when motor interlock is enabled (throttle hold off). RC Passthrough sends the input from the RC Motor Interlock channel as throttle output. External Gov SetPoint sends the RSC SetPoint parameter value as throttle output. Throttle Curve uses the 5 point throttle curve to determine throttle output based on the collective output. AutoThrottle requires a rotor speed sensor, contains an advanced autothrottle governor and is primarily for piston and turbine engines. WARNING: Throttle ramp time and throttle curve MUST be tuned properly using Throttle Curve mode before using AutoThrottle

params.name: H_RSC_RAMP_TIME
params.desc_en: Time in seconds for throttle output (HeliRSC servo) to ramp from ground idle (RSC_IDLE) to flight idle throttle setting when motor interlock is enabled (throttle hold off).

params.name: H_RSC_RUNUP_TIME
params.desc_en: Actual time in seconds for the main rotor to reach full speed after motor interlock is enabled (throttle hold off). Must be at least one second longer than the Throttle Ramp Time that is set with RSC_RAMP_TIME. WARNING: For AutoThrottle users with piston and turbine engines it is VERY important to know how long it takes to warm up your engine and reach full rotor speed when throttle switch is turned ON. This timer should be set for at least the amount of time it takes to get your helicopter to full flight power, ready for takeoff. Failure to heed this warning could result in the auto-takeoff mode attempting to lift up into hover before the engine has reached full power, and subsequent loss of control

params.name: H_RSC_SETPOINT
params.desc_en: Throttle (HeliRSC Servo) output in percent to the external motor governor when motor interlock enabled (throttle hold off).

params.name: H_RSC_SLEWRATE
params.desc_en: This controls the maximum rate at which the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) can change, as a percentage per second. A value of 100 means the throttle can change over its full range in one second. A value of zero gives unlimited slew rate.

params.name: H_RSC_THRCRV_0
params.desc_en: Sets the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) in percent for the throttle curve at the minimum collective pitch position. The 0 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MIN. Example: if the setup has -2 degree to +10 degree collective pitch setup, this setting would correspond to -2 degree of pitch.

params.name: H_RSC_THRCRV_100
params.desc_en: Sets the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) in percent for the throttle curve at the minimum collective pitch position. The 100 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MAX. Example: if the setup has -2 degree to +10 degree collective pitch setup, this setting would correspond to +10 degree of pitch.

params.name: H_RSC_THRCRV_25
params.desc_en: Sets the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) in percent for the throttle curve at 25% of full collective travel where he 0 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MIN and 100 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MAX. Example: if the setup has -2 degree to +10 degree collective pitch setup, the total range is 12 degrees. 25% of 12 degrees is 3 degrees, so this setting would correspond to +1 degree of pitch.

params.name: H_RSC_THRCRV_50
params.desc_en: Sets the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) in percent for the throttle curve at 50% of full collective travel where he 0 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MIN and 100 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MAX. Example: if the setup has -2 degree to +10 degree collective pitch setup, the total range is 12 degrees. 50% of 12 degrees is 6 degrees, so this setting would correspond to +4 degree of pitch.

params.name: H_RSC_THRCRV_75
params.desc_en: Sets the throttle output (HeliRSC servo) in percent for the throttle curve at 75% of full collective travel where he 0 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MIN and 100 percent collective is defined by H_COL_MAX. Example: if the setup has -2 degree to +10 degree collective pitch setup, the total range is 12 degrees. 75% of 12 degrees is 9 degrees, so this setting would correspond to +7 degree of pitch.

params.name: H_SV_MAN
params.desc_en: Manual servo override for swash set-up. Must be 0 (Disabled) for flight!

params.name: H_SV_TEST
params.desc_en: Number of cycles to run servo test on boot-up

params.name: H_SW2_COL_DIR
params.desc_en: Direction collective moves for positive pitch. 0 for Normal, 1 for Reversed

params.name: H_SW2_H3_ENABLE
params.desc_en: Automatically set when H3 generic swash type is selected for swashplate 2. Do not set manually.

params.name: H_SW2_H3_PHANG
params.display: Swash 2 H3 Generic Phase Angle Comp
params.desc_en: Only for H3 swashplate. If pitching the swash forward induces a roll, this can be correct the problem

params.name: H_SW2_H3_SV1_POS
params.desc_en: Azimuth position on swashplate for servo 1 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

params.name: H_SW2_H3_SV2_POS
params.desc_en: Azimuth position on swashplate 2 for servo 2 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

params.name: H_SW2_H3_SV3_POS
params.desc_en: Azimuth position on swashplate 2 for servo 3 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

params.name: H_SW2_LIN_SVO
params.desc_en: This linearizes the swashplate 2 servo's mechanical output to account for nonlinear output due to arm rotation. This requires a specific setup procedure to work properly. The servo arm must be centered on the mechanical throw at the servo trim position and the servo trim position kept as close to 1500 as possible. Leveling the swashplate can only be done through the pitch links. See the ardupilot wiki for more details on setup.

params.name: H_SW2_TYPE
params.desc_en: H3 is generic, three-servo only. H3_120/H3_140 plates have Motor1 left side, Motor2 right side, Motor3 elevator in rear. HR3_120/HR3_140 have Motor1 right side, Motor2 left side, Motor3 elevator in front - use H3_120/H3_140 and reverse servo and collective directions as necessary. For all H3_90 swashplates use H4_90 and don't use servo output for the missing servo. For H4-90 Motors1&2 are left/right respectively, Motors3&4 are rear/front respectively. For H4-45 Motors1&2 are LF/RF, Motors3&4 are LR/RR

params.name: H_SW_COL_DIR
params.desc_en: Direction collective moves for positive pitch. 0 for Normal, 1 for Reversed

params.name: H_SW_H3_ENABLE
params.desc_en: Automatically set when H3 generic swash type is selected for swashplate 1. Do not set manually.

params.name: H_SW_H3_PHANG
params.display: Swash 1 H3 Generic Phase Angle Comp
params.desc_en: Only for H3 swashplate. If pitching the swash forward induces a roll, this can be correct the problem

params.name: H_SW_H3_SV1_POS
params.desc_en: Azimuth position on swashplate for servo 1 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

params.name: H_SW_H3_SV2_POS
params.desc_en: Azimuth position on swashplate 1 for servo 2 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

params.name: H_SW_H3_SV3_POS
params.desc_en: Azimuth position on swashplate 1 for servo 3 with the front of the heli being 0 deg

params.name: H_SW_LIN_SVO
params.desc_en: This linearizes the swashplate 1 servo's mechanical output to account for nonlinear output due to arm rotation. This requires a specific setup procedure to work properly. The servo arm must be centered on the mechanical throw at the servo trim position and the servo trim position kept as close to 1500 as possible. Leveling the swashplate can only be done through the pitch links. See the ardupilot wiki for more details on setup.

params.name: H_SW_TYPE
params.desc_en: H3 is generic, three-servo only. H3_120/H3_140 plates have Motor1 left side, Motor2 right side, Motor3 elevator in rear. HR3_120/HR3_140 have Motor1 right side, Motor2 left side, Motor3 elevator in front - use H3_120/H3_140 and reverse servo and collective directions as necessary. For all H3_90 swashplates use H4_90 and don't use servo output for the missing servo. For H4-90 Motors1&2 are left/right respectively, Motors3&4 are rear/front respectively. For H4-45 Motors1&2 are LF/RF, Motors3&4 are LR/RR

params.name: H_TAIL_SPEED
params.desc_en: Direct drive, variable pitch tail ESC speed in percent output to the tail motor esc (HeliTailRSC Servo) when motor interlock enabled (throttle hold off) and speed fully ramped up after spoolup.

params.name: H_TAIL_TYPE
params.desc_en: Tail type selection. Servo Only uses tail rotor pitch to provide yaw control (including stabilization) via an output assigned to Motor4. Servo with External Gyro uses an external gyro to control tail rotor pitch via a servo. Yaw control without stabilization is passed to the external gyro via the output assigned to Motor4. Direct Drive Variable Pitch(DDVP) is used for tails that have a motor whose ESC is connected to an output with function HeliTailRSC. Tail pitch is still accomplished with a servo on an output assigned to Motor4 function. Direct Drive Fixed Pitch (DDFP) CW is used for helicopters with a rotor that spins clockwise when viewed from above with a motor whose ESC is controlled by an output whose function is Motor4. Direct Drive Fixed Pitch (DDFP) CCW is used for helicopters with a rotor that spins counter clockwise when viewed from above with a motor whose ESC is controlled by an output whose function is Motor4. In both DDFP cases, no servo is used for the tail and the tail motor esc on Motor4 output is used to control the yaw axis using motor speed.

params.name: H_YAW_REV_EXPO
params.desc_en: For intermeshing mode only. Yaw revereser smoothing exponent, smoothen transition near zero collective region. Increase this parameter to shink smoothing range. Set to -1 to disable reverser.

params.name: H_YAW_SCALER
params.desc_en: Scaler for mixing yaw into roll or pitch.

params.name: H_YAW_TRIM
params.desc_en: Fixed offset applied to yaw output to minimize yaw I-term contribution needed to counter rotor drag. Currently only works for DDFP tails (H_TAIL_TYPE = 3 or H_TAIL_TYPE = 4). If using the H_COL2YAW compensation this trim is used to compensate for the main rotor profile drag. If H_COL2YAW is not used, this value can be set to reduce the yaw I-term to zero when in a steady hover. In this case, move trim in the direction of the I-term found in PIDY.I log message (e.g. negative I means you want negative trim).

params.name: IM_ACRO_COL_EXP
params.desc_en: Used to soften collective pitch inputs near center point in Acro mode.

params.name: IM_STB_COL_1
params.desc_en: Helicopter's minimum collective pitch setting at zero collective stick input in Stabilize mode. Set this as a percent of collective range given by H_COL_MAX minus H_COL_MIN.

params.name: IM_STB_COL_2
params.desc_en: Helicopter's collective pitch setting at mid-low (40%) collective stick input in Stabilize mode. Set this as a percent of collective range given by H_COL_MAX minus H_COL_MIN.

params.name: IM_STB_COL_3
params.desc_en: Helicopter's collective pitch setting at mid-high (60%) collective stick input in Stabilize mode. Set this as a percent of collective range given by H_COL_MAX minus H_COL_MIN.

params.name: IM_STB_COL_4
params.desc_en: Helicopter's maximum collective pitch setting at full collective stick input in Stabilize mode. Set this as a percent of collective range given by H_COL_MAX minus H_COL_MIN.

params.name: INS_HNTC2_ATT
params.desc_en: Harmonic Notch Filter attenuation in dB. Values greater than 40dB will typically produce a hard notch rather than a modest attenuation of motor noise.

params.name: INS_HNTC2_BW
params.desc_en: Harmonic Notch Filter bandwidth in Hz. This is typically set to half the base frequency. The ratio of base frequency to bandwidth determines the notch quality factor and is fixed across harmonics.

params.name: INS_HNTC2_ENABLE
params.desc_en: Harmonic Notch Filter enable

params.name: INS_HNTC2_FM_RAT
params.desc_en: The minimum ratio below the configured frequency to take throttle based notch filters when flying at a throttle level below the reference throttle. Note that lower frequency notch filters will have more phase lag. If you want throttle based notch filtering to be effective at a throttle up to 30% below the configured notch frequency then set this parameter to 0.7. The default of 1.0 means the notch will not go below the frequency in the FREQ parameter.

params.name: INS_HNTC2_FREQ
params.desc_en: Harmonic Notch Filter base center frequency in Hz. This is the center frequency for static notches, the center frequency for Throttle based notches at the reference thrust value, and the minimum limit of center frequency variation for all other notch types. This should always be set lower than half the backend gyro rate (which is typically 1Khz).

params.name: INS_HNTC2_HMNCS
params.desc_en: Bitmask of harmonic frequencies to apply Harmonic Notch Filter to. This option takes effect on the next reboot. A value of 0 disables this filter. The first harmonic refers to the base frequency.

params.name: INS_HNTC2_MODE
params.display: Harmonic Notch Filter dynamic frequency tracking mode
params.desc_en: Harmonic Notch Filter dynamic frequency tracking mode. Dynamic updates can be throttle, RPM sensor, ESC telemetry or dynamic FFT based. Throttle-based harmonic notch cannot be used on fixed wing only planes. It can for Copters, QuadPlane(while in VTOL modes), and Rovers.

params.name: INS_HNTC2_OPTS
params.desc_en: Harmonic Notch Filter options. Triple and double-notches can provide deeper attenuation across a wider bandwidth with reduced latency than single notches and are suitable for larger aircraft. Multi-Source attaches a harmonic notch to each detected noise frequency instead of simply being multiples of the base frequency, in the case of FFT it will attach notches to each of three detected noise peaks, in the case of ESC it will attach notches to each of four motor RPM values. Loop rate update changes the notch center frequency at the scheduler loop rate rather than at the default of 200Hz. If both double and triple notches are specified only double notches will take effect.

bitmask.en: Use min freq on RPM source failure

params.name: INS_HNTC2_REF
params.desc_en: A reference value of zero disables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter and a positive value enables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter. For throttle-based scaling, this parameter is the reference value associated with the specified frequency to facilitate frequency scaling of the Harmonic Notch Filter. For RPM and ESC telemetry based tracking, this parameter is set to 1 to enable the Harmonic Notch Filter using the RPM sensor or ESC telemetry set to measure rotor speed. The sensor data is converted to Hz automatically for use in the Harmonic Notch Filter. This reference value may also be used to scale the sensor data, if required. For example, rpm sensor data is required to measure heli motor RPM. Therefore the reference value can be used to scale the RPM sensor to the rotor RPM.

params.name: INS_HNTC3_OPTS
params.desc_en: Harmonic Notch Filter options. Triple and double-notches can provide deeper attenuation across a wider bandwidth with reduced latency than single notches and are suitable for larger aircraft. Multi-Source attaches a harmonic notch to each detected noise frequency instead of simply being multiples of the base frequency, in the case of FFT it will attach notches to each of three detected noise peaks, in the case of ESC it will attach notches to each of four motor RPM values. Loop rate update changes the notch center frequency at the scheduler loop rate rather than at the default of 200Hz. If both double and triple notches are specified only double notches will take effect.

bitmask.en: Use min freq on RPM source failure

params.name: INS_HNTC3_REF
params.desc_en: A reference value of zero disables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter and a positive value enables dynamic updates on the Harmonic Notch Filter. For throttle-based scaling, this parameter is the reference value associated with the specified frequency to facilitate frequency scaling of the Harmonic Notch Filter. For RPM and ESC telemetry based tracking, this parameter is set to 1 to enable the Harmonic Notch Filter using the RPM sensor or ESC telemetry set to measure rotor speed. The sensor data is converted to Hz automatically for use in the Harmonic Notch Filter. This reference value may also be used to scale the sensor data, if required. For example, rpm sensor data is required to measure heli motor RPM. Therefore the reference value can be used to scale the RPM sensor to the rotor RPM.

params.name: INS_HNTC4_ATT
params.desc_en: Harmonic Notch Filter attenuation in dB. Values greater than 40dB will typically produce a hard notch rather than a modest attenuation of motor noise.

params.name: INS_HNTC4_BW
params.desc_en: Harmonic Notch Filter bandwidth in Hz. This is typically set to half the base frequency. The ratio of base frequency to bandwidth determines the notch quality factor and is fixed across harmonics.

params.name: INS_HNTC4_ENABLE
params.desc_en: Harmonic Notch Filter enable

params.name: INS_HNTC4_FM_RAT
params.desc_en: The minimum ratio below the configured frequency to take throttle based notch filters when flying at a throttle level below the reference throttle. Note that lower frequency notch filters will have more phase lag. If you want throttle based notch filtering to be effective at a throttle up to 30% below the configured notch frequency then set this parameter to 0.7. The default of 1.0 means the notch will not go below the frequency in the FREQ parameter.

params.name: INS_HNTC4_FREQ
params.desc_en: Harmonic Notch Filter base center frequency in Hz. This is the center frequency for static notches, the center frequency for Throttle based notches at the reference thrust value, and the minimum limit of center frequency variation for all other notch types. This should always be set lower than half the backend gyro rate (which is typically 1Khz).

params.name: INS_HNTC4_HMNCS
params.desc_en: Bitmask of harmonic frequencies to apply Harmonic Notch Filter to. This option takes effect on the next reboot. A value of 0 disables this filter. The first harmonic refers to the base frequency.

params.name: INS_HNTC4_MODE
params.display: Harmonic Notch Filter dynamic frequency tracking mode
params.desc_en: Harmonic Notch Filter dynamic frequency tracking mode. Dynamic updates can be throttle, RPM sensor, ESC telemetry or dynamic FFT based. Throttle-based harmonic notch cannot be used on fixed wing only planes. It can for Copters, QuadPlane(while in VTOL modes), and Rovers.

params.name: INS_POS1_X
params.desc_en: X position of the first IMU Accelerometer in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin. Attention: The IMU should be located as close to the vehicle c.g. as practical so that the value of this parameter is minimised. Failure to do so can result in noisy navigation velocity measurements due to vibration and IMU gyro noise. If the IMU cannot be moved and velocity noise is a problem, a location closer to the IMU can be used as the body frame origin.

params.display: Stillness threshold for detecting if we are moving
params.desc_en: Threshold to tolerate vibration to determine if vehicle is motionless. This depends on the frame type and if there is a constant vibration due to motors before launch or after landing. Total motionless is about 0.05. Suggested values: Planes/rover use 0.1, multirotors use 1, tradHeli uses 5

params.name: LAND_ALT_LOW_M
params.desc_en: Altitude during Landing at which vehicle slows to LAND_SPD_MS

params.name: LAND_REPOSITION
params.desc_en: Enables user input during LAND mode, the landing phase of RTL, and auto mode landings.

params.name: LAND_SPD_HIGH_MS
params.desc_en: The descent speed for the first stage of landing in m/s. If this is zero then WP_SPD_DN is used

params.name: LAND_SPD_MS
params.desc_en: The descent speed for the final stage of landing in m/s

params.name: LGR_DEPLOY_ALT
params.desc_en: Altitude where the landing gear will be deployed. This should be lower than the RETRACT_ALT. If zero then altitude is not used for deploying landing gear. Only applies when vehicle is armed.

params.name: LGR_DEPLOY_PIN
params.desc_en: Pin number to use for detection of gear deployment. If set to -1 feedback is disabled. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

params.name: LGR_DEPLOY_POL
params.desc_en: Polarity for feedback pin. If this is 1 then the pin should be high when gear are deployed. If set to 0 then then deployed gear level is low.

params.name: LGR_ENABLE
params.desc_en: Enable landing gear control

params.name: LGR_OPTIONS
params.desc_en: Options to retract or deploy landing gear in Auto or Guided mode

params.name: LGR_RETRACT_ALT
params.desc_en: Altitude where the landing gear will be retracted. This should be higher than the DEPLOY_ALT. If zero then altitude is not used for retracting landing gear. Only applies when vehicle is armed.

params.name: LGR_STARTUP
params.desc_en: Landing Gear Startup behaviour control

params.name: LGR_WOW_PIN
params.desc_en: Pin number to use for feedback of weight on wheels condition. If set to -1 feedback is disabled. Some common values are given, but see the Wiki's "GPIOs" page for how to determine the pin number for a given autopilot.

params.name: LGR_WOW_POL
params.display: Weight on wheels feedback pin polarity
params.desc_en: Polarity for feedback pin. If this is 1 then the pin should be high when there is weight on wheels. If set to 0 then then weight on wheels level is low.

params.name: LOG_BACKEND_TYPE
params.desc_en: Bitmap of what Logger backend types to enable. Block-based logging is available on SITL and boards with dataflash chips. Multiple backends can be selected.

params.name: LOG_BITMASK
params.desc_en: Bitmap of what on-board log types to enable. This value is made up of the sum of each of the log types you want to be saved. It is usually best just to enable all basiclog types by setting this to 65535. Note that if you want to reduce log sizes you should consider using LOG_FILE_RATEMAX instead of disabling logging items with this parameter.

params.name: LOG_BLK_RATEMAX
params.display: Maximum logging rate for block backend
params.desc_en: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the block backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

params.name: LOG_DARM_RATEMAX
params.desc_en: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to any backend when disarmed. A value of zero means that the normal backend rate limit is applied.

params.name: LOG_DISARMED
params.desc_en: If LOG_DISARMED is set to 1 then logging will be enabled at all times including when disarmed. Logging before arming can make for very large logfiles but can help a lot when tracking down startup issues and is necessary if logging of EKF replay data is selected via the LOG_REPLAY parameter. If LOG_DISARMED is set to 2, then logging will be enabled when disarmed, but not if a USB connection is detected. This can be used to prevent unwanted data logs being generated when the vehicle is connected via USB for log downloading or parameter changes. If LOG_DISARMED is set to 3 then logging will happen while disarmed, but if the vehicle never arms then the logs using the filesystem backend will be discarded on the next boot.

values.en: Discard log on reboot if never armed

params.name: LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE
params.display: Logging File and Block Backend buffer size max (in kibibytes)
params.desc_en: The File and Block backends use a buffer to store data before writing to the block device. Raising this value may reduce "gaps" in your SD card logging but increases memory usage. This buffer size may be reduced to free up available memory

params.name: LOG_FILE_DSRMROT
params.display: Stop logging to current file on disarm
params.desc_en: When set, the current log file is closed when the vehicle is disarmed. If LOG_DISARMED is set then a fresh log will be opened. Applies to the File and Block logging backends.

params.name: LOG_FILE_MB_FREE
params.display: Old logs on the SD card will be deleted to maintain this amount of free space
params.desc_en: Set this such that the free space is larger than your largest typical flight log

params.name: LOG_FILE_RATEMAX
params.display: Maximum logging rate for file backend
params.desc_en: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the file backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

params.name: LOG_FILE_TIMEOUT
params.display: Timeout before giving up on file writes
params.desc_en: This controls the amount of time before failing writes to a log file cause the file to be closed and logging stopped.

params.name: LOG_MAV_BUFSIZE
params.display: Maximum AP_Logger MAVLink Backend buffer size
params.desc_en: Maximum amount of memory to allocate to AP_Logger-over-mavlink

params.name: LOG_MAV_RATEMAX
params.display: Maximum logging rate for mavlink backend
params.desc_en: This sets the maximum rate that streaming log messages will be logged to the mavlink backend. A value of zero means that rate limiting is disabled.

params.name: LOG_MAX_FILES
params.desc_en: This sets the maximum number of log file that will be written on dataflash or sd card before starting to rotate log number. Limit is capped at 500 logs.

params.name: LOG_REPLAY
params.display: Enable logging of information needed for Replay
params.desc_en: If LOG_REPLAY is set to 1 then the EKF2 and EKF3 state estimators will log detailed information needed for diagnosing problems with the Kalman filter. LOG_DISARMED must be set to 1 or 2 or else the log will not contain the pre-flight data required for replay testing of the EKF's. It is suggested that you also raise LOG_FILE_BUFSIZE to give more buffer space for logging and use a high quality microSD card to ensure no sensor data is lost.

params.name: LOIT_ACC_MAX_M
params.desc_en: Loiter maximum correction acceleration in m/s/s. Higher values cause the copter to correct position errors more aggressively.

params.name: LOIT_ANG_MAX
params.desc_en: Loiter maximum pilot requested lean angle. Set to zero for 2/3 of PSC_ANGLE_MAX/ATC_ANGLE_MAX. The maximum vehicle lean angle is still limited by PSC_ANGLE_MAX/ATC_ANGLE_MAX

params.name: LOIT_BRK_ACC_M
params.desc_en: Loiter braking acceleration in m/s/s. Higher values stop the copter more quickly when the stick is centered.

params.name: LOIT_BRK_DELAY
params.desc_en: Loiter brake start delay (in seconds)

params.name: LOIT_BRK_JRK_M
params.desc_en: Loiter braking jerk in m/s/s/s. Higher values will remove braking faster if the pilot moves the sticks during a braking maneuver.

params.name: LOIT_OPTIONS
params.desc_en: Enables optional Loiter mode behaviors

params.name: LOIT_SPEED_MS
params.desc_en: Defines the maximum speed in m/s which the aircraft will travel horizontally while in loiter mode

params.name: LTE_BAND
params.desc_en: This allows selection of LTE band. A value of -1 means no band setting change is made. A value of 0 sets all bands. Otherwise the specified band is set.

params.name: LTE_BAUD
params.desc_en: Baud rate for the serial port to the LTE modem when connected. Initial power on baudrate is in LTE_IBAUD

params.name: LTE_ENABLE
params.desc_en: Enable or disable the LTE modem driver

params.name: LTE_IBAUD
params.desc_en: This is the initial baud rate on power on for the modem. This is set in the modem with the AT+IREX=baud command

params.name: LTE_MCCMNC
params.desc_en: This allows selection of network operator

params.name: LTE_OPTIONS
params.desc_en: Options to control the LTE modem driver. If VerboseSignalInfoGCS is set then additional NAMED_VALUE_FLOAT values are sent with verbose signal information

params.name: LTE_PROTOCOL
params.desc_en: The protocol that we will use in communication with the LTE modem. If this is PPP then the LTE_SERVER parameters are not used and instead a PPP connection will be established and you should use the NET_ parameters to enable network ports. If this is MAVLink2 then the LTE_SERVER parameters are used to create a TCP or UDP connection to a single server.

params.name: LTE_SCRPORT
params.desc_en: Scripting Serial port to use for the LTE modem. This is the index of the SCR_SDEV ports that are set to 2 for "MAVLink2"

params.name: LTE_SERPORT
params.desc_en: Serial port to use for the LTE modem. This is the index of the SERIALn_ ports that are set to 28 for "scripting"

params.name: LTE_SERVER_IP0
params.desc_en: First octet of the server IP address to connect to

params.name: LTE_SERVER_IP1
params.desc_en: Second octet of the server IP address to connect to

params.name: LTE_SERVER_IP2
params.desc_en: Third octet of the server IP address to connect to

params.name: LTE_SERVER_IP3
params.desc_en: Fourth octet of the server IP address to connect to

params.name: LTE_SERVER_PORT
params.desc_en: IPv4 Port of the server to connect to

params.name: LTE_TIMEOUT
params.desc_en: Timeout in seconds for the LTE connection. If no data is received for this time, the connection will be reset. A value of zero disables the timeout

params.name: LTE_TX_RATE
params.desc_en: Maximum data transmit rate to the modem in bytes/second. Use zero for unlimited

params.name: MAV_GCS_SYSID
params.desc_en: This sets what MAVLink source system IDs are accepted for GCS failsafe handling, RC overrides and manual control. When MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI is less than MAV_GCS_SYSID then only this value is considered to be a GCS. When MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI is greater than or equal to MAV_GCS_SYSID then the range of values between MAV_GCS_SYSID and MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI (inclusive) are all treated as valid GCS MAVLink system IDs

params.name: MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI
params.desc_en: Upper limit of MAVLink source system IDs considered to be from the GCS. When this is less than MAV_GCS_SYSID then only MAV_GCS_SYSID is used as GCS ID. When this is greater than or equal to MAV_GCS_SYSID then the range of values from MAV_GCS_SYSID to MAV_GCS_SYSID_HI (inclusive) is treated as a GCS ID.

params.name: MAV_OPTIONS
params.desc_en: Alters various behaviour of the MAVLink interface

bitmask.en: Accept MAVLink only from system IDs given by MAV_SYSID_GCS and MAV_SYSID_GCS_HI

params.name: MAV_SYSID
params.display: MAVLink system ID of this vehicle
params.desc_en: Allows setting an individual MAVLink system id for this vehicle to distinguish it from others on the same network.

params.name: MAV_TELEM_DELAY
params.desc_en: The amount of time (in seconds) to delay radio telemetry to prevent an Xbee bricking on power up

params.name: MIS_OPTIONS
params.desc_en: Bitmask of what options to use in missions. If the DontZeroCounter counter option is set than on completion of a jump loop the counter is left at zero, so the jump will not happen again if the loop is re-entered.

params.name: MIS_RESTART
params.display: Mission Restart when entering Auto mode
params.desc_en: Controls mission starting point when entering Auto mode (either restart from beginning of mission or resume from last command run)

params.name: MIS_TOTAL
params.desc_en: The number of mission mission items that has been loaded by the ground station. Do not change this manually.

params.name: MNT1_DEFLT_MODE
params.desc_en: Mount default operating mode on startup and after control is returned from autopilot

params.name: MNT1_DEVID
params.desc_en: Mount device ID, taking into account its type, bus and instance

params.name: MNT1_LEAD_PTCH
params.desc_en: Servo mount pitch angle output leads the vehicle angle by this amount of time based on current pitch rate. Increase until the servo is responsive but does not overshoot

params.name: MNT1_LEAD_RLL
params.desc_en: Servo mount roll angle output leads the vehicle angle by this amount of time based on current roll rate. Increase until the servo is responsive but does not overshoot

params.name: MNT1_NEUTRAL_X

params.desc_en: Battery voltage compensation maximum voltage (voltage above this will have no additional scaling effect on thrust). Recommend 4.2 * cell count, 0 = Disabled

params.desc_en: Battery voltage compensation minimum voltage (voltage below this will have no additional scaling effect on thrust). Recommend 3.3 * cell count, 0 = Disabled

params.desc_en: Booster motor output scaling factor vs main throttle. The output to the BoostThrottle servo will be the main throttle times this scaling factor. params.desc_en: Delay after reaching ground idle when armed to allow ESC startup to complete.

params.desc_en: Motor options

params.name: MOT_PWM_MAX
params.desc_en: This sets the max PWM value in microseconds that will ever be output to the motors

params.name: MOT_PWM_MIN
params.desc_en: This sets the min PWM output value in microseconds that will ever be output to the motors

params.name: MOT_PWM_TYPE
params.desc_en: This selects the output PWM type, allowing for normal PWM continuous output, OneShot, brushed or DShot motor output.PWMRange and PWMAngle are PWM special/rare cases for ESCs that dont calibrate normally (some Sub motors) or where each ESC must have its PWM range set individually using the Servo params instead of PWM_MIN/MAX parameters.

params.name: MOT_SAFE_DISARM

params.name: MOT_SAFE_TIME

params.desc_en: Delay after arming before spool transitions are allowed, used to let ESCs/servos complete startup when PWM was disabled while disarmed.

params.name: MOT_SLEW_DN_TIME
params.display: Output slew time for decreasing throttle
params.desc_en: Time in seconds to slew output from full to zero. This is used to limit the rate at which output can change. Range is constrained between 0 and 0.5.

params.name: MOT_SLEW_UP_TIME
params.display: Output slew time for increasing throttle
params.desc_en: Time in seconds to slew output from zero to full. This is used to limit the rate at which output can change. Range is constrained between 0 and 0.5.

params.name: MOT_SPIN_ARM
params.desc_en: Point at which the motors start to spin expressed as a number from 0 to 1 in the entire output range. Should be lower than MOT_SPIN_MIN.

params.name: MOT_SPIN_MAX
params.desc_en: Point at which the thrust saturates expressed as a number from 0 to 1 in the entire output range

params.name: MOT_SPIN_MIN
params.desc_en: Point at which the thrust starts expressed as a number from 0 to 1 in the entire output range. Should be higher than MOT_SPIN_ARM.

params.name: MOT_SPOOL_TIME
params.desc_en: Time in seconds to spool up the motors from zero to min throttle.

params.name: MOT_SPOOL_TIM_DN
params.desc_en: Time to ramp the throttle ceiling down toward zero. If 0, SPOOL_TIME is used.

params.name: MOT_THST_EXPO
params.desc_en: Motor thrust curve exponent (0.0 for linear to 1.0 for second order curve)

params.name: MOT_THST_HOVER
params.desc_en: Motor thrust needed to hover expressed as a number from 0 to 1

params.name: MOT_YAW_HEADROOM
params.desc_en: Yaw control is given at least this pwm in microseconds range

params.name: MOT_YAW_SV_ANGLE

params.name: NTF_LED_LEN
params.desc_en: The number of Serial LED's to use for notifications (NeoPixel's and ProfiLED)

params.name: NTF_LED_OVERRIDE
params.display: Specifies colour source for the RGBLed
params.desc_en: Specifies the source for the colours and brightness for the LED. OutbackChallenge conforms to the MedicalExpress (https://uavchallenge.org/medical-express/) rules, essentially "Green" is disarmed (safe-to-approach), "Red" is armed (not safe-to-approach). Traffic light is a simplified color set, red when armed, yellow when the safety switch is not surpressing outputs (but disarmed), and green when outputs are surpressed and disarmed, the LED will blink faster if disarmed and failing arming checks.

params.name: NTF_LED_TYPES
params.desc_en: Controls what types of LEDs will be enabled

params.name: OA_BR_CONT_RATIO
params.display: Obstacle Avoidance margin ratio for BendyRuler to change bearing significantly
params.desc_en: BendyRuler will avoid changing bearing unless ratio of previous margin from obstacle (or fence) to present calculated margin is atleast this much.

params.name: OA_BR_TYPE

params.name: OA_DB_ALT_MIN
params.display: OADatabase minimum altitude above home before storing obstacles
params.desc_en: OADatabase will reject obstacles if vehicle's altitude above home is below this parameter, in a 3 meter radius around home. Set 0 to disable this feature.

params.name: OA_DB_BEAM_WIDTH
params.desc_en: Beam width of incoming lidar data, used to calculate a object radius if none is provided by the data source.

params.name: OA_DB_DIST_MAX
params.desc_en: Maximum distance of objects held in database. Set to zero to disable the limits

params.name: OA_DB_EXPIRE
params.desc_en: OADatabase item timeout. The time an item will linger without any updates before it expires. Zero means never expires which is useful for a sent-once static environment but terrible for dynamic ones.

params.name: OA_DB_OUTPUT
params.desc_en: OADatabase output level to configure which database objects are sent to the ground station. All data is always available internally for avoidance algorithms.

values.en: Send HIGH and NORMAL importance items

params.name: OA_DB_QUEUE_SIZE
params.display: OADatabase queue maximum number of points
params.desc_en: OADatabase queue maximum number of points. This in an input buffer size. Larger means it can handle larger bursts of incoming data points to filter into the database. No impact on cpu, only RAM. Recommend larger for faster datalinks or for sensors that generate a lot of data.

params.name: OA_DB_RADIUS_MIN
params.desc_en: Minimum radius of objects held in database

params.name: OA_DB_SIZE
params.desc_en: OADatabase maximum number of points. Set to 0 to disable the OA Database. Larger means more points but is more cpu intensive to process

params.name: OA_MARGIN_MAX

params.name: OSD_ARM_SCR
params.desc_en: Screen to be shown on Arm event. Zero to disable the feature.

params.name: OSD_BTN_DELAY
params.desc_en: Debounce time in ms for stick commanded parameter navigation.

params.name: OSD_CELL_COUNT
params.desc_en: Used for average cell voltage display. -1 disables, 0 uses cell count autodetection for well charged LIPO/LIION batteries at connection, other values manually select cell count used.

params.name: OSD_CHAN
params.desc_en: This sets the channel used to switch different OSD screens.

params.name: OSD_DSARM_SCR
params.desc_en: Screen to be shown on disarm event. Zero to disable the feature.

params.name: OSD_FONT
params.desc_en: This sets which OSD font to use. It is an integer from 0 to the number of fonts available

params.name: OSD_FS_SCR
params.desc_en: Screen to be shown on failsafe event. Zero to disable the feature.

params.name: OSD_H_OFFSET
params.desc_en: Sets horizontal offset of the osd inside image

params.name: OSD_MSG_TIME
params.desc_en: Sets message duration seconds

params.name: OSD_OPTIONS
params.desc_en: This sets options that change the display

bitmask.en: Convert feet to miles at 5280ft instead of 10000ft

params.name: OSD_SB_H_OFS
params.desc_en: Extends the spacing between the sidebar elements by this amount of columns. Positive values increases the width to the right of the screen.

params.name: OSD_SB_V_EXT
params.desc_en: Increase of vertical length of the sidebar itens by this amount of lines. Applied equally both above and below the default setting.

params.name: OSD_SW_METHOD
params.desc_en: This sets the method used to switch different OSD screens.

values.en: switch to next screen if channel value was changed
select screen based on pwm ranges specified for each screen
switch to next screen after low to high transition and every 1s while channel value is high

params.name: OSD_TYPE
params.desc_en: OSD type. TXONLY makes the OSD parameter selection available to other modules even if there is no native OSD support on the board, for instance CRSF.

params.name: OSD_TYPE2
params.desc_en: OSD type 2. TXONLY makes the OSD parameter selection available to other modules even if there is no native OSD support on the board, for instance CRSF.

params.name: OSD_UNITS
params.desc_en: Sets the units to use in displaying items

params.name: OSD_V_OFFSET
params.desc_en: Sets vertical offset of the osd inside image

params.name: OSD_W_ACRVOLT
params.display: Avg Cell Resting Volt warn level
params.desc_en: Set level at which ACRVOLT item will flash

params.name: OSD_W_AVGCELLV
params.desc_en: Set level at which AVGCELLV item will flash

params.name: OSD_W_BATVOLT
params.desc_en: Set level at which BAT_VOLT item will flash

params.name: OSD_W_LQ
params.desc_en: Set level at which RC_LQ item will flash (%)

params.name: OSD_W_NSAT
params.desc_en: Set level at which NSAT item will flash

params.name: OSD_W_RESTVOLT
params.desc_en: Set level at which RESTVOLT item will flash

params.name: OSD_W_RSSI
params.desc_en: Set level at which RSSI item will flash (in positive % or negative dBm values as applicable). 30% or -100dBm are defaults.

params.name: OSD_W_SNR
params.desc_en: Set level at which RC_SNR item will flash (in db)

params.name: OSD_W_TERR
params.desc_en: Set level below which TER_HGT item will flash. -1 disables.

params.name: PARAM_LOCK_ENAB
params.desc_en: Param Lockdown enable

params.name: PHLD_BRK_ANGLE
params.desc_en: PosHold flight mode's max lean angle during braking in degrees

params.name: PHLD_BRK_RATE
params.desc_en: PosHold flight mode's rotation rate during braking in deg/sec

params.name: PILOT_ACC_Z
params.desc_en: The vertical acceleration used when pilot is controlling the altitude

params.name: PILOT_SPD_DN
params.desc_en: The maximum vertical descending velocity the pilot may request in m/s. If 0 PILOT_SPD_UP value is used.

params.name: PILOT_SPD_UP
params.desc_en: The maximum vertical ascending velocity the pilot may request in m/s

params.name: PILOT_THR_BHV
params.desc_en: Bitmask containing various throttle stick options. TX with sprung throttle can set PILOT_THR_BHV to "1" so motor feedback when landed starts from mid-stick instead of bottom of stick.

params.name: PILOT_THR_FILT
params.desc_en: Throttle filter cutoff (Hz) - active whenever altitude control is inactive - 0 to disable

params.name: PILOT_TKO_ALT_M
params.desc_en: Altitude that altitude control modes will climb to when a takeoff is triggered with the throttle stick.

params.name: PILOT_Y_EXPO
params.desc_en: Pilot controlled yaw expo to allow faster rotation when stick at edges

params.name: PILOT_Y_RATE
params.desc_en: Pilot controlled yaw rate max. Used in all pilot controlled modes except Acro

params.name: PILOT_Y_RATE_TC
params.display: Pilot yaw rate control input time constant
params.desc_en: Pilot yaw rate control input time constant. Low numbers lead to sharper response, higher numbers to softer response

params.name: PLDP_DELAY
params.desc_en: Delay after release, in seconds, before aircraft starts to climb back to starting altitude.

params.name: PLDP_RNG_MAX
params.display: Payload Place maximum range finder altitude
params.desc_en: Maximum range finder altitude in m to trigger payload touchdown, set to zero to disable.

params.name: PLDP_SPEED_DN
params.desc_en: The maximum vertical decent velocity in m/s. If 0 LAND_SPD_MS value is used.

params.name: PLDP_THRESH
params.desc_en: Ratio of vertical thrust during decent below which payload touchdown will trigger.

params.name: PLND_ACC_P_NSE
params.desc_en: Kalman Filter Accelerometer Noise, higher values weight the input from the camera more, accels less

params.name: PLND_ALT_CUTOFF
params.desc_en: The altitude (rangefinder distance) below which we stop using the precision landing sensor and continue landing

params.name: PLND_ALT_MAX
params.desc_en: Vehicle will continue landing vertically until this height if target is not found. Below this height if landing target is not found, landing retry/failsafe might be attempted. This needs a rangefinder to work. Set to zero to disable this.

params.name: PLND_ALT_MIN
params.desc_en: Vehicle will continue landing vertically even if target is lost below this height. This needs a rangefinder to work. Set to zero to disable this.

params.name: PLND_BUS
params.desc_en: Precland sensor bus for I2C sensors.

params.name: PLND_CAM_POS_X
params.desc_en: X position of the camera in body frame. Positive X is forward of the origin.

params.name: PLND_CAM_POS_Y
params.desc_en: Y position of the camera in body frame. Positive Y is to the right of the origin.

params.name: PLND_CAM_POS_Z
params.desc_en: Z position of the camera in body frame. Positive Z is down from the origin.

params.name: PLND_ENABLED
params.desc_en: Precision Land enabled/disabled

params.name: PLND_EST_TYPE
params.desc_en: Specifies the estimation method to be used

params.name: PLND_LAG
params.desc_en: Precision Landing sensor lag, to cope with variable landing_target latency

params.name: PLND_LAND_OFS_X
params.desc_en: Desired landing position of the camera forward of the target in vehicle body frame

params.name: PLND_LAND_OFS_Y
params.desc_en: desired landing position of the camera right of the target in vehicle body frame

params.name: PLND_OPTIONS
params.desc_en: Precision Landing Extra Options

bitmask.en: Allow Precision Landing after manual reposition
Maintain high speed in final descent

params.name: PLND_RET_BEHAVE
params.desc_en: Prec Land will do the action selected by this parameter if a retry to a landing is needed

values.en: Go to the last location where landing target was detected
Go towards the approximate location of the detected landing target

params.name: PLND_RET_MAX
params.display: PrecLand Maximum number of retires for a failed landing
params.desc_en: PrecLand Maximum number of retires for a failed landing. Set to zero to disable landing retry.

params.name: PLND_STRICT
params.desc_en: How strictly should the vehicle land on the target if target is lost

params.name: PLND_TIMEOUT
params.desc_en: Time for which vehicle continues descend even if target is lost. After this time period, vehicle will attempt a landing retry depending on PLND_STRICT parameter.

params.name: PLND_TYPE
params.desc_en: Precision Land Type

params.name: PLND_XY_DIST_MAX
params.display: Precision Landing maximum distance to target before descending
params.desc_en: The vehicle will not start descending if the landing target is detected and it is further than this many meters away. Set 0 to always descend.

params.name: PLND_YAW_ALIGN
params.desc_en: Yaw angle from body x-axis to sensor x-axis.

params.name: POI_DIST_MAX
params.desc_en: POI's max distance (in meters) from the vehicle

params.name: PORT
params.desc_en: Which Scripting serial port the sensor is connected at.

params.name: PREV_ENABLE
params.desc_en: Enable parameter reversion system

params.name: PREV_RC_FUNC
params.desc_en: RCn_OPTION number to used to trigger parameter reversion

params.desc_en: Minimum expected range for Proximity Sensor. Setting this to 0 will set value to manufacturer reported range.

params.name: PRX5_ORIENT
params.desc_en: Proximity sensor orientation

params.name: PRX5_RECV_ID
params.desc_en: The receive ID of the CAN frames. A value of zero means all IDs are accepted.

params.name: PRX5_TYPE
params.desc_en: What type of proximity sensor is connected

params.name: PRX5_YAW_CORR
params.desc_en: Proximity sensor yaw correction

params.name: PRX_ALT_MIN
params.desc_en: Minimum altitude below which proximity should not work.

params.name: PRX_FILT
params.desc_en: Cutoff frequency for low pass filter applied to each face in the proximity boundary

params.name: PRX_IGN_GND
params.desc_en: Ignore proximity data that is within 1 meter of the ground below the vehicle. This requires a downward facing rangefinder

params.name: PRX_LOG_RAW
params.desc_en: Set this parameter to one if logging unfiltered(raw) distances from sensor should be enabled

params.name: PSC_ANGLE_MAX
params.desc_en: Maximum lean angle autopilot can request. Set to zero to use ANGLE_MAX parameter value

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_D
params.desc_en: Acceleration (vertical) controller D gain. Compensates for short-term change in desired vertical acceleration vs actual acceleration. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_D * 0.1.

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_D_FF
params.desc_en: FF D Gain which produces an output that is proportional to the rate of change of the target. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_P * 0.1.

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_FF
params.desc_en: Acceleration (vertical) controller feed forward. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_FF * 0.1.

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_FLTD
params.display: Acceleration (vertical) controller derivative frequency in Hz
params.desc_en: Acceleration (vertical) controller derivative frequency in Hz. Previously _ACCZ_FLTD.

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_FLTE
params.display: Acceleration (vertical) controller error frequency in Hz
params.desc_en: Acceleration (vertical) controller error frequency in Hz. Previously _ACCZ_FLTE.

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_FLTT
params.display: Acceleration (vertical) controller target frequency in Hz
params.desc_en: Acceleration (vertical) controller target frequency in Hz. Previously _ACCZ_FLTT.

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_I
params.desc_en: Acceleration (vertical) controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired vertical acceleration and actual acceleration. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_I * 0.1.

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_IMAX
params.desc_en: Acceleration (vertical) controller I gain maximum. Constrains the maximum pwm that the I term will generate. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_IMAX * 0.001.

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_NEF
params.desc_en: Accel (vertical) Error notch filter index. If upgrading from 4.6 this is Previously _ACCZ_NEF.

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_NTF
params.desc_en: Accel (vertical) Target notch filter index. If upgrading from 4.6 this is Previously _ACCZ_NTF.

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_P
params.desc_en: Acceleration (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical acceleration and actual acceleration into a motor output. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_P * 0.1.

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_PDMX
params.desc_en: Acceleration (vertical) controller PD sum maximum. The maximum/minimum value that the sum of the P and D term can output. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _ACCZ_P * 0.1.

params.name: PSC_D_ACC_SMAX
params.desc_en: Sets an upper limit on the slew rate produced by the combined P and D gains. If the amplitude of the control action produced by the rate feedback exceeds this value, then the D+P gain is reduced to respect the limit. This limits the amplitude of high frequency oscillations caused by an excessive gain. The limit should be set to no more than 25% of the actuators maximum slew rate to allow for load effects. Note: The gain will not be reduced to less than 10% of the nominal value. A value of zero will disable this feature.

params.name: PSC_D_JERK
params.display: Jerk limit for the vertical kinematic input shaping
params.desc_en: Jerk limit of the vertical kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the aircraft varies the acceleration target

params.name: PSC_D_POS_P
params.desc_en: Position (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between the desired altitude and actual altitude into a climb or descent rate which is passed to the throttle rate controller. Previously _POSZ_P.

params.name: PSC_D_VEL_D
params.desc_en: Velocity (vertical) controller D gain. Corrects short-term changes in velocity. Previously _VELZ_D.

params.name: PSC_D_VEL_FF
params.desc_en: Velocity (vertical) controller Feed Forward gain. Produces an output that is proportional to the magnitude of the target. Previously _VELZ_FF.

params.name: PSC_D_VEL_FLTD
params.display: Velocity (vertical) input filter for D term
params.desc_en: Velocity (vertical) input filter for D term. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for D terms. Previously _VELZ_FLTD.

params.name: PSC_D_VEL_FLTE
params.desc_en: Velocity (vertical) error filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for P and I terms. Previously _VELZ_FLTE.

params.name: PSC_D_VEL_I
params.desc_en: Velocity (vertical) controller I gain. Corrects long-term difference in desired velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELZ_I.

params.name: PSC_D_VEL_IMAX
params.desc_en: Velocity (vertical) controller I gain maximum. Constrains the target acceleration that the I gain will output. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _VELZ_IMAX * 0.01.

params.name: PSC_D_VEL_P
params.desc_en: Velocity (vertical) controller P gain. Converts the difference between desired vertical speed and actual speed into a desired acceleration that is passed to the throttle acceleration controller. Previously _VELZ_P.

params.name: PSC_NE_JERK
params.display: Jerk limit for the horizontal kinematic input shaping
params.desc_en: Jerk limit of the horizontal kinematic path generation used to determine how quickly the aircraft varies the acceleration target

params.name: PSC_NE_POS_P
params.desc_en: Position controller P gain. Converts the distance (in the latitude direction) to the target location into a desired speed which is then passed to the loiter latitude rate controller. Previously _POSXY_P.

params.name: PSC_NE_VEL_D
params.desc_en: Velocity (horizontal) D gain. Corrects short-term changes in velocity. Previously _VELXY_D.

params.name: PSC_NE_VEL_FF
params.desc_en: Velocity (horizontal) feed forward gain. Converts the difference between desired velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELXY_FF.

params.name: PSC_NE_VEL_FLTD
params.desc_en: Velocity (horizontal) input filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for D term. Previously _VELXY_FLTD.

params.name: PSC_NE_VEL_FLTE
params.desc_en: Velocity (horizontal) input filter. This filter (in Hz) is applied to the input for P and I terms. Previously _VELXY_FLTE.

params.name: PSC_NE_VEL_I
params.desc_en: Velocity (horizontal) I gain. Corrects long-term difference between desired and actual velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELXY_I.

params.name: PSC_NE_VEL_IMAX
params.desc_en: Velocity (horizontal) integrator maximum. Constrains the target acceleration that the I gain will output. If upgrading from 4.6 this is _VELXY_IMAX * 0.01.

params.name: PSC_NE_VEL_P
params.desc_en: Velocity (horizontal) P gain. Converts the difference between desired and actual velocity to a target acceleration. Previously _VELXY_P.

params.name: QUIK_ANGLE_MAX
params.display: maximum angle error for tune abort
params.desc_en: If while tuning the angle error goes over this limit then the tune will aborts to prevent a bad oscillation in the case of the tuning algorithm failing. If you get an error "Tuning: attitude error ABORTING" and you think it is a false positive then you can either raise this parameter or you can try increasing the QUIK_DOUBLE_TIME to do the tune more slowly. A value of zero disables this check.

params.name: QUIK_AUTO_FILTER
params.desc_en: When enabled the PID filter settings are automatically set based on INS_GYRO_FILTER

params.name: QUIK_AUTO_SAVE
params.desc_en: Number of seconds after completion of tune to auto-save. This is useful when using a 2 position switch for quicktune

params.name: QUIK_AXES
params.desc_en: axes to tune

params.name: QUIK_DOUBLE_TIME
params.desc_en: Time to double a tuning parameter. Raise this for a slower tune.

params.name: QUIK_ENABLE
params.desc_en: Enable quicktune system

params.name: QUIK_GAIN_MARGIN
params.desc_en: Reduction in gain after oscillation detected. Raise this number to get a more conservative tune

params.name: QUIK_MAX_REDUCE
params.desc_en: This controls how much quicktune is allowed to lower gains from the original gains. If the vehicle already has a reasonable tune and is not oscillating then you can set this to zero to prevent gain reductions. The default of 20% is reasonable for most vehicles. Using a maximum gain reduction lowers the chance of an angle P oscillation happening if quicktune gets a false positive oscillation at a low gain, which can result in very low rate gains and a dangerous angle P oscillation.

params.name: QUIK_OPTIONS
params.desc_en: Additional options. When the Two Position Switch option is enabled then a high switch position will start the tune, low will disable the tune. you should also set a QUIK_AUTO_SAVE time so that you will be able to save the tune.

params.name: QUIK_OSC_SMAX
params.desc_en: Threshold for oscillation detection. A lower value will lead to a more conservative tune.

params.name: QUIK_RC_FUNC
params.desc_en: RCn_OPTION number to use to control tuning stop/start/save

params.name: QUIK_RP_PI_RATIO
params.desc_en: Ratio between P and I gains for roll and pitch. Raise this to get a lower I gain

params.name: QUIK_YAW_D_MAX
params.desc_en: Maximum value for yaw D gain

params.name: QUIK_YAW_P_MAX
params.desc_en: Maximum value for yaw P gain

params.name: QUIK_Y_PI_RATIO
params.desc_en: Ratio between P and I gains for yaw. Raise this to get a lower I gain

params.name: RALLY_INCL_HOME
params.desc_en: Controls if Home is included as a Rally point (i.e. as a safe landing place) for RTL

params.name: RALLY_LIMIT_KM
params.desc_en: Maximum distance to rally point. If the closest rally point is more than this number of kilometers from the current position and the home location is closer than any of the rally points from the current position then do RTL to home rather than to the closest rally point. This prevents a leftover rally point from a different airfield being used accidentally. If this is set to 0 then the closest rally point is always used.

params.name: RALLY_TOTAL
params.desc_en: Number of rally points currently loaded
